Edible High vs Smoking High

For regular cannabis consumers, it is common knowledge that an edible high is going to feel different than a smoking high. What's not commonly known is that edibles feel different because the THC is actually different.

When you smoke or vaporize THC, you're getting Delta-9 THC. When you eat or drink cannabis, that Delta-9 THC is metabolized through your liver and transformed into 11-Hydroxy-THC before it hits your bloodstream. In other words, edible highs feel different because they are different. You're experiencing a different kind of cannabinoid.
Final thoughts

Cannabis edibles offer a convenient and discreet way to consume cannabinoids for both recreational and medicinal purposes. By understanding how they're made, dosing considerations, potential effects, and safety tips, you can enjoy edibles responsibly and make informed choices that enhance your cannabis experience. Remember to start low, go slow, and always prioritize safety and moderation.
Can I make my own edibles?

You can absolutely make your own edibles. All you need is some activated cannabis oil and a recipe. You'll need to consider the temperature at which you are cooking and how you will make sure the cannabis oil gets evenly distributed throughout the recipe. If it sounds too complicated or you don't have the time, you can always buy precision-dosed, lab-tested, delicious products from your local cannabis shop.
Do you sell CBD-only edibles?

We sell a variety of edibles in different dosages and ratios. Most options will include trace amounts of THC, but not all will produce intoxicating effects (individual results may vary). If you're looking to avoid effects, you'll want to pick an edible with a high CBD to THC ratio (20:1, 10:1) and/or find an edible that has 1mg or less of THC. You can find hemp-derived CBD products at your local corner store (thanks to the 2018 Farm Bill), but they are not required to go through the same testing and oversight as products in licensed cannabis shops. If you want a consistent and clean product, it is best to get your CBD products from a cannabis shop.
What's the difference between CBD and THC edibles?

In short. THC is going to produce an intoxicating effect, and CBD is going be psychoactive but not intoxicating. Most edibles from cannabis shops are going to have a mix of CBD and THC. Edibles that contain less than 1mg of THC typically will not produce a noticeable intoxicating effect. Also, CBD is legal in more states than THC. So be sure to check your local laws before purchasing or carrying products with THC.
What do edibles taste like?

Some edibles will produce a strong cannabis flavor, and others will not. It is going to depend on the type of cannabis product that was used to infuse the edible. Edibles that include distillate are going to produce a minimal cannabis flavor, but their effects are not going to be as robust as cannabis oils that are full-spectrum. Edibles made with more full-spectrum oils are going to produce a more complex effect, but they can also have a strong cannabis flavor.
How should I store my edibles?

Like all food products, they're going to have a shelf life. The ingredients in your edibles are going to go bad before the cannabis degrades, so be sure to use best practices when it comes to storing your edibles. Store them away from sunlight and avoid extreme temperatures.
How long have edibles existed?

Edibles have a long history that extends across the globe. Bhang is a traditional drink from India that has been around for over a thousand years. It is typically consumed as a celebration during the spring festivals of Maha Shivaratri and Holi. More recently, pot brownies came to the forefront of culture in the United States during the 60's.

What cultural traditions or values from your Hispanic heritage do you bring into your work at Sunnyside*?​

I had a relentless work ethic instilled in me at a very young age. I began working in the family business as a way to spend more time with my family when I was a child, and learned the value of a dollar earned through hard work. I carry that work ethic with me every day inside and outside of work for the benefit of my team, my family, and myself.​
What advice would you give to other Hispanic individuals who are interested in pursuing a career in the cannabis industry?​

Don't give up. Like many of us, it took me a few years before finding an opportunity in the industry, but when you're in, the ball is in your court. Learn everything you can, bring your personal experience and style, and make the most of every opportunity. "Si tu puedes!" ​
What cultural traditions or values from your Hispanic heritage do you bring into your work at Sunnyside*?​

Hispanic culture contains something called personalismo. This is a term for the importance of personal connections with others where there is a caring, trusting, and warm personal relationship. It is based on a perception that each person truly cares about the well-being of the other person. I care about my team. It's important to me to check in with them, talk to them, get to know them.​
What advice would you give to other Hispanic individuals who are interested in pursuing a career in the cannabis industry?​

Here is some history: Nearly a century ago, U.S. federal lawmakers began to examine cannabis legislation, which eventually led to its prohibition in 1937. The reason? At that time, an influx of Mexican immigrants were entering the country following the Mexican Revolution, bringing with them bits of their culture, which included “marihuana,”. The flow of new immigrants brought a wave of xenophobia, which eventually led to the demonization of cannabis as a way to quell Hispanics entering the country. We have come so far. Time to break the stigma and give knowledge to all people in the world.​
How do you celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month, and how does it inspire your work?​

I love to cook! Cooking is not just about eating, it's an art and means a lot to me to feed everyone. I love to bring in food for the team. I also love to talk about my family and nationality. I'm a proud Boricua, Portuguese, Spanish woman.​
What cultural traditions or values from your Hispanic heritage do you bring into your work at Sunnyside*?​
As a Boricua, I bring el “sazon” to the store sometimes!​
What advice would you give to other Hispanic individuals who are interested in pursuing a career in the cannabis industry?​
Know about the state's [cannabis] regulations, have a good product knowledge about what you are growing or selling. Being bilingual is a plus too!​
How do you celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month, and how does it inspire your work?​
I celebrate it every day. I'm a very proud Puerto Rican, especially now that I just moved to the US!​

title: Live Resin vs Rosin
description: Let's talk about the key differences between Live Resin and Live Rosin.

data.text: What's the difference between live resin and live rosin?

Let's get to know the difference between the two. Both are "Live", meaning they're created from cannabis plants flash frozen immediately after being cut down. A big contrast from traditional drying and curing methods, which can degrade cannabinoids and trichomes—resulting in loss of potency, aroma, and flavor.

This Live process is the ideal way to preserve the plant's trichomes, where all the cannabinoids and terpenes live. Think of your cannabis experience as a car: THC is your gas pedal, and terpenes and minor cannabinoids are your steering wheel. Now, let's shine some light on the differences between Live Resin and Live Rosin so you can find a product that fits your lifestyle.

data.alt: What's the difference between live resin and live rosin?

data.text: What is Live Resin?
Both Live Resin and Live Rosin are available in similar forms like concentrates, vapes, and edibles but it's their extraction process that differentiates the two.

With Live Resin, fresh frozen cannabis plants are put through a solvent extraction process which utilizes butane, propane, CO2, or another solvent. This dissolves all the trichomes—but since the process works like a chemical magnet, it can favor certain compounds and leave others behind.

The extracted oil can then be developed into gummies, vape cartridges, and various concentrates like glassy shatter. You can expect a flavorful and potent cannabis experience at a good price point. “With live resin, we’re harvesting flower at its peak freshness. We freeze it in that state and then extract it in that state, so we can provide the best representation of what that particular flower strain actually is. By contrast, think about buying out-of-season vegetables at a supermarket. If you bought frozen vegetables instead, they’d be fresher because they were chopped and frozen right at peak performance time, rather than sitting on a truck, going through oxidation, and sitting in the market. The plant loses some of its flavor because it’s gone through that process.” - Tyler Finnen, Director of Manufacturing, Cresco Labs.
Shop Live Resin

data.alt: "With live resin, we're harvesting flower at its peak freshness." – Tyler Finnen, Director of Manufacturing

data.text: What is Live Rosin?

Live Rosin offers a more pure, refined, representation of the plant by using a solventless ice water extraction. This unique process collects the same ratio of cannabinoids/terpene that the original plant offers.

Live Rosin extraction is more intensive and time-consuming than Live Resin extraction, but the end result is a more complex, nuanced flavor profile, a smoother consumption experience, and a cleaner/more robust edible.

Plus, Live Rosin doesn't use chemical solvents, so it's considered a more natural, clean product. Think of your usual THC experience as watching a movie on TV, but Live Rosin is like watching it in a 3D movie theater.
What are the different forms of Live Rosin?
You can enjoy the full-spectrum benefits of Live Rosin in a variety of cannabis products like concentrates, vapes, and edibles.

Pro tip: always store Rosin concentrates and vapes in the fridge to best savor the flavor and potency of this labor of love. And be sure to store your vapes upright! "It’s kind of like a wine–you want to keep it in a cool, dark place like a wine cellar. Oxidation and heat are the enemy. I actually have a refrigerator at home where I store my live resins and rosins…that’s how you want to preserve the terpenes.” - Tyler Finnen, Director of Manufacturing, Cresco Labs
Concentrates

Concentrates are known to provide a stronger experience that's true to the plant's terpene profile. Jam concentrate has a fruit preserve-like consistency with mouth-watering aromas. Badder is a smooth and creamy concentrate that's easier to handle than jam. Bubble Hash appears light blonde to dark brown and is developed using ice water, agitation, and then filtered out using a set of bubble wash bags.

Now that you've got your concentrate, how are you going to enjoy it? You'll need a dab rig or dab pen to achieve the correct temperature, but some adventurous connoisseurs add them to flower pre-rolls and bowls. You can expect THCa percentages from the mid 70s to upper 80s and above. Note: Concentrates are not available in all markets. Check your local menu for availability.
Shop Live Rosin Concentrates
What are live rosin vapes?

Want to enjoy live rosin in an easier to use form? Check out a live rosin vape cartridge. You'll fully appreciate the plant's complete flavor profile through smooth, potent hits—creating a harmonious high. The ice water extraction method ensures you're tasting maximum terpenes and cannabinoids; never leftover plant material. All you need is a vape battery to get started. For the best flavor and experience, we recommend using a battery that has multiple heat settings and using it on low so you don't toast your vape cart. Note: Live Rosin vapes are currently available in Illinois, Arizona, Florida, and Massachusetts. Stay tuned for new live rosin products at your local store.
Shop Live Rosin Vapes
What are live rosin edibles?

To truly savor the innovation of Live Rosin, try a bite in edible form. Live Rosin edibles capture all the nuance and flavor of the trichomes without any unwanted taste. Plus, they offer full-spectrum benefits which reflect the optimal potency, terpene, flavonoid, and cannabinoid profiles of each strain. Because of this, you can expect a wider spectrum of psychotropic and physiological effects than regular distillate edibles, unlocking the full potential of the plant.
Shop Live Rosin Edibles
Note: Live Rosin edibles are currently available in Illinois only. If you’re not in Illinois, stay tuned for new live rosin products at your local store.
Which one is right for you?

If Live Resin is a science, Live Rosin is an art form. Now that you know Live Resin from Live Rosin, it really comes down to personal preference and what works for you. To get started, check our live menus for the latest cutting-edge Live Rosin vapes, edibles, and concentrates.

When a cannabis plant has been flash frozen immediately after harvest to preserve the maximum number of terpenes and cannabinoids, instead of the traditional curing and drying process.

Solvent-based extractions use a solvent like butane, propane, or CO2 to extract oil from fresh frozen cannabis.
What does solventless mean?
Solventless means using an ice-water extraction in conjunction with heat and pressure to extract cannabis oil, an all-natural process with no chemicals added.

Full-spectrum products mean that all the trichomes of the cannabis plant are preserved—and the full potential of psychotropic and physiological effects are unlocked.

title: Strain HIGHlight: Pineapple Express
description: Let's learn more about one of the most popular marijuana strains, Pineapple Express.

data.text: Hollywood has given fans of cannabis many treats over the years, but perhaps none more special than the 2008 comedy, Pineapple Express. But what’s even better is that this strain always lives up to the hype. Its electric effects, incredible flavors and aromas, and beautiful buds make this hybrid worthy of all its accolades.
What is the Pineapple Express strain?

items: Most phenotypes are bred by crossing Trainwreck (a sativa-dominant hybrid) with Hawaiian (a sativa), creating a sativa-leaning hybrid.
Pineapple Express’s average THC content hovers around 25-31%, making it a great choice for anyone seeking a potent experience.
This strain went from being very popular in California dispensaries to one of the most well-known strains in America.
The most common terpenes present in Pineapple Express are terpinolene , ocimene , and myrcene .

data.text: Where did the Pineapple Express strain Come From?

Named after a weather phenomenon where there’s an increase in the flow of moisture around Hawaii and the north Pacific coast (objectively a pretty funny thing to name a strain after), Seth Rogen said in 2018 that no such strain existed. G13 Labs claims to have been the originator of the first Pineapple Express flowers, but the history is a bit hazy. Either way, it didn’t take much time for this strain to skyrocket in popularity.

items: Parent lineage: a cross between Trainwreck and Hawaiian

data.text: How is Pineapple Express grown?

"Pineapple Express is grown under the same standard operating procedure as all Cresco strains across the nation. We use sterile growing methods that limit the introduction of pathogens and fungi, precision irrigation via root zone monitoring that allow us to determine exactly how much each strain eats/drinks and give each variety exactly what it wants." - Jeremy Thompson , VP Technical Cultivation

“Growing it in production and breeding with it has been a treat! When we get a look at it today, it certainly checks all the boxes we look for when selecting phenos. The potency always tests out for the range we are looking for as well. This strain was an easy addition to the menu and any time I want to get a high-yielding, fruity terpene, this is the #1 choice. It has also been in production for 6 years, being one of the oldest strains we grow!"

“For growing, this strain has performed well in multiple different media types; it can be grown in soil, rockwool, and coco coir and it still manages to retain all the things we love about it! Its yielding potential is nothing to shake a stem at, capable of yielding ¾ - 1lb of dried flower per plant! Cloning time is 17 days, harvest can be at 60 days but can go to as late as 65 with no issues, the drying process we would want wrapped up around 7 days, any longer and the plant gets a bit too dry.” - Tyler Solis , Genetic Research & Development Lead
What does Pineapple Express Smell and Taste Like?

Pineapple Express has one of the most famous bouquets of aromas and flavors. Upon cracking open your dram, citrusy notes of lemon and lime jump forward, followed by a sweet, earthiness that even flirts a little bit with funkiness. It has tastes of sweeter citrus and tropical fruits, like pineapple and mango, backed up by a cedarlike woodiness.

“The unique pineapple and tropical aroma can get even the most seasoned smoker excited for a great initial uplifting experience followed by a smooth, relaxing come down.” - Tyler Solis , Genetic Research & Development Lead
What is Pineapple Express good for?

Pineapple Express creates a generally uplifted feeling: it provides an energetic boost, a feeling of happiness and being present in the moment. This makes it a great strain for daytime use and social settings as you won’t be risking a truly sedating experience.

The three main terpenes present in Pineapple Express are terpinolene , ocimene , and myrcene . Each terpene contributes to the incredible profile that makes up this legendary strain. This is known as the entourage effect, where the copresence of terpenes and THC generates a larger experience than just being high.
Terpinolene is known to have floral, pine flavors and aromas, as well as antioxidant properties, providing stress relief, and aiding sleep.*
Ocimene is known to have sweet, herbaceous, citrus, and woody flavors and aromas, as well as anti-inflammatory properties.*
Myrcene is known to be responsible for clove and herbal flavors and aromas, as well as aiding sleep, anti-inflammatory properties, and analgesic effects.*
*individual results may vary

Cresco has been growing Pineapple Express since before 2017 and it’s been a staple of ours ever since.
Check your local Sunnyside dispensary menu’s flower, concentrate, or vape section and search for ‘pineapple express.’ Our wellness advisors can also help you find Pineapple Express you need in store.

Is Pineapple Express strong?
Averaging around 25% THC, it starts to approach a strong experience.
Is Pineapple Express Sativa or Indica?
It’s a sativa-dominant hybrid, coming in at 70% sativa and 30% indica.
What Flavor is Pineapple Express?
Pineapple Express has a sweet, tropical fruit flavor that’s followed by woody notes.
What does Pineapple Express look like?
Classic olive green nugs are absolutely covered in dusky orange hairs and shiny trichomes.

data.text: Where did the Bio Jesus strain come from?

data.text: How is Bio Jesus grown?

"We grow Bio Jesus indoors, hydroponically in stone wool substrate. It grows slowly and it’s a bit sensitive to water, so we take substrate sensors that plug into the root zone directly and relay back information on exactly how much food and water is in that root zone.

We also cater our irrigations to Bio J’s specific requirements with our nutrient formula – because that formula has nitrogen in it, which Bio J is sensitive to, the cloning and rooting phase can sometimes be tricky. Bio Jesus is a very old genetic and it’s a low-yielding plant. It's also a pure indica, which means it's short and squatty. We don’t typically top, or pinch, that type of plant - we just let it grow straight up.

Cannabis connoisseurs swear by it, and with good reason; there’s more flavor, more aromas, and a truer representation of strains than you’ll get with a pre-roll, edible, or other forms of vape-able cannabis extracts. And that pure product can lead to pure bliss.
The Basics: What is Live Resin?

We live in a farm-to-table era, so you probably know from having squeezed lemonade, made guacamole, or even just visiting a farmers market, that there’s no substitute for using fresh, organic ingredients straight from the source. It’s no different when it comes to our favorite crop, you guessed it , cannabis. You’ll always want your cannabis to be harvested at its peak ripeness and perfectly preserved right until the moment your session starts. Cresco Liquid Live Resin hits all of these beats, without artificial additives or fillers, so to understand this top-shelf form of consumption, here’s the practical facts you need to know about LLR, no biochemistry doctorate required, we promise. Liquid Live Resin is a cannabis concentrate , a liquid derived from having reduced plant material down to its most potent parts. Not unlike the amber that captured dinosaur DNA in Jurassic Park (shoutout to Dr. John Hammond), resin is secreted from cannabis and contains a bevy of good stuff, like terpenes, cannabinoids, and flavonoids it’s the coveted crown jewel of the plant. These naturally occurring compounds give cannabis its flavor profile, the equivalent of grape tannins in wine production, along with a full spectrum of effects. "Live resin is the Rolex of cannabis — it's the true flavor of the plant. I'd rather have live resin over flower—over anything...because you’re capturing the best representation of that plant, literally frozen in time.” - Tyler Finnen, Director of Manufacturing, Cresco Labs

data.text: Why Consider Consuming Liquid Live Resin?
There’s a litany of reasons you should reach for LLR on your next dispensary visit, these are just a few unique ways it makes for an enhanced experience:
Top-Shelf Quality and Flavor

While potent products are appealing, LLR also balances your high with a smooth, flavorful consumption experience (note: your individual results may vary). Other concentrates are commonly reconstituted, "strain flavored," and engineered from pieces and parts resulting in loss of complexity. Not the case with Cresco Liquid Live Resin, as Tamer Mohamed, VP of Manufacturing, East Region at Cresco Labs puts it: “the mouthfeel is a lot richer than a normal distillate vape where you might be getting burnt terpenes or a rubbery taste. With LLR the taste is elevated, you’re not coughing your face off after a three-second draw and you’re able to taste a good amount of the flavor on the way out.”
Full Spectrum Cannabis

The cannabis plant itself has a full spectrum of hundreds of chemical compounds that offer up a variety of effects and benefits. Even other full spectrum products produced out of dry plant material can result in the loss of some valuable terpenes. Cresco Liquid Live Resin contains all of the compounds that were available at the moment of harvest and consuming it brings the plant’s unique potential to life. “Our live resin is full spectrum. What that means is you’re getting everything out of the plant…a whole entourage effect of other compounds. So not only the minors, but the majors too. And by combining those, you get the best of both worlds. That’s the great thing about different cannabis strains: each one offers its own symphony of minor cannabinoids and terpenes, providing unique effects.” - Tyler Finnen, Director of Manufacturing, Cresco Labs.
High Potency

Cresco LLR is derived from pure, raw, cannabis, meaning that it’s high in THC content. For comparison, an average cannabis plant can contain up to 25% THC. With live resins, it can be as much as 80-90% THC offering more punch per puff.
Preserved Strain Characteristics

Live resins offer up a more strain-specific experience to users than many other concentrates or edibles. By freezing the flower, LLR captures the true nature of the flower and strain in a cartridge without adding a single additional component to it. “You’re going to get the unadulterated version of cannabis flower” says David Sanchez, VP of Manufacturing, West Region at Cresco Labs. “We’re here to present the plant as purely as possible, we’re not going to outdo Mother Nature in a lab.” Tyler Finnen agrees: "Live resin can preserve terpenes even better than dry flower. If you’ve ever walked into a grow room during peak harvest, the terpene smell smacks you in the face before you even get in the door. But if you walk into a dry room, it’s going to smell more green and more grassy, because it’s just going through that drying process.”
The Benefits of Vaping

Vaping as your primary method of choice makes sense as Cresco LLR carts make for a convenient and discrete cannabis experience. Your vape is ready whenever you want to session, it’s portable and can be easily tucked away on the go. There is also an appeal for users who prefer to inhale vapor rather than smoke.
Fine-tuning Your Experience

Consuming cannabis is all about customizing your experience to cater to your individual needs. Finding the right cannabinoid ratio and terpene profile increasingly is the way that both medical and recreational customers shop. Coming in a variety of strain profiles, Cresco Liquid Live Resin makes it easy to hone on which mix of cannabinoids fit you best.

data.text: How is Liquid Live Resin Made?

When producing LLR, the main goal is to capture the pure essence of the live cannabis plant, so after harvesting, the delicate process skips the typical stages of drying and curing and instead flash-freezes the plant material at -80 Celsius in order to best preserve the delicate flavors. From there, liquid butane is used to carefully transfer all the aforementioned terps, cannabinoids, and flavonoids until it’s later purged, leaving only the live resin in concentrate form. The end product will be tested by third party labs to ensure the absence of residual solvents, microbials, and heavy metals, and tabulate the total terpenes and THC/CBD content. Tyler Finnen says, "We grow to peak freshness, we harvest at peak ripeness, and we freeze it right away—when it’s been harvested. We extract our material frozen to preserve the terpenes. We really take our time, gently activating our material so we’re not boiling off terpenes. We’re focused on preserving the true essence of the plant. The saying is, ‘gold in, gold out’. We’re extracting that plant, taking nothing out, and putting nothing back in. It’s the true essence of what a grow is. And the benefit is: the true, full-spectrum effects of a strain can be preserved.”

It's certainly a meticulous craft, one you might compare to making coffee, which also happens to be a liquid extraction (science!). Liquid Live Resin is like pour-over coffee, it's far and away the best, purest method for capturing the complexities of your key ingredient, allowing the flavors and aromas to shine through. The extraction of both resin and coffee preserves the essence of its ingredients, whether bud or beans, artfully infusing the oils, fragrances, and flavor molecules into the final product. And what about distillates that aren't held to the same rigorous quality standards of LLR? Well, you know that sad pot of stale drip coffee sitting on the hot plate at your office? That’s the equivalent risk you run consuming cannabis distillates. “Liquid live resin is the closest essence to the flower possible. It’s not going to be a fake, artificial, fruity flavor—it’s going to be extremely cannabis-forward with flavors that you’d expect to smell or taste in the plant itself.” - Matt Brown, Director of Manufacturing, Cresco Labs.

title: How to Clean a Bong
description: By regularly cleaning your bong, you can remove buildup, impress your friends, and enjoy a cleaner, more flavorful, fully potent smoke.

data.text: Keeping your bong and all of its components clean is crucial to enjoying cannabis to its fullest. When you use a bong or glassware to consume flower, tar and resin build up because of combustion—which can affect the taste of your smoke, and may reduce your overall enjoyment of a smoking session.

If left uncleaned for long enough, your dirty bong water can also begin to grow mold inside (yuck). By regularly cleaning your bong, you can remove buildup, impress your friends, and enjoy a cleaner, more flavorful, fully potent smoke.
Here’s instructions on how to clean your bong and what you’ll need to clean it.
Supplies will include:

items: Isopropyl alcohol (preferably 70% or higher, 91% is a great choice)
Coarse salt (we recommend Epsom salt)
Paper towels
Q-Tips or pipe cleaners (for hard-to-reach spots)
Ziplocks
Rubber bands/hair ties

data.text: Step 1: Get ready for Cleaning

Head to the bathroom with all your materials and pieces. The first step in cleaning your bong is to disassemble it so that everything can be washed individually. Depending on the type of bong or glassware you have, this could involve separating and removing the bowl, downstem, and base. Make sure to keep each piece organized so you can reassemble the bong or glassware correctly.
Step 2: Rinse the Pieces with Hot Water

After you've disassembled the bong into its parts, rinse each piece with hot water. This will help to remove any loose debris and make what remains easier to remove, making the cleaning process more effective.
Step 3: Add Coarse Salt and Alcohol
After removing as much water as possible, pour a generous amount of coarse salt into the base of the bong, followed by enough isopropyl alcohol to cover the salt.
The salt will act as an abrasive, while the alcohol will dissolve the tar and resin buildup.

Place your bowl and downstem in separate bags, add about a tablespoon of salt and enough isopropyl to cover it. Seal the bags, give each one a good shake for roughly 30 seconds, and let them soak for a while.
Step 4: Plug the Openings of the Bong or Glassware

Cover the openings of the bong with your hands, fashion covers out of ziplocks and rubber bands, or rubber stoppers to seal them. This will prevent the salt and alcohol from spilling out while you shake the bong.
Step 5: Shake the Bong or Bags with Glassware

Really shake the bong so that the salt and alcohol mixture cleans the interior of the piece. Shaking creates friction between the salt and the interior of the pieces, which will remove buildup. While shaking up and down will normally get most residue removed, tilt the bong towards any dirtier areas and resume vigorous shaking.
If necessary, repeat this step a few times until the inside of your bong is clean.
After letting the bowl and downstem soak for a long time, shake it again and rinse with hot water.

Be sure to only place one glass element in a Ziploc bag by itself, to avoid breaking fragile glass parts.

Pro tip: Res Tips are extra absorbent swabs perfect for use on bongs. “One end has an enlarged tip with plenty of surface area to soak up residue, while the other tapered end is perfect for tedious, hard-to-reach parts of your piece." — Tyler Schmid, Randy's​ ​

data.text: Step 6: Rinse with Hot Water One More Time
If your piece is looking shiny and new, run hot water through each piece to remove any remaining salt/alcohol. Rinse each piece thoroughly to ensure that all the residue is removed.
Step 7: Dry the Pieces
Use paper towels to dry each piece thoroughly. Make sure that each piece is dry before reassembling the bong.
Step 8: Reassemble the Bong
Put the pieces back together, making sure that they are snug and secure.
After you complete the bong cleaning process, you’re ready to enjoy a cleaner, fuller, fresher smoke.

data.text: How do I clean acrylic bongs? Is it the same process?

You’ll start by disassembling and rinsing, just like you would with glass. Once you’ve dried it, then you’ll do your best to lightly coat the inside with baking soda, place it into a container or bag for 10-15 minutes, and soak it in white vinegar for another 10 minutes. From there—rinse, scrub, and rinse again! Dry and enjoy.
What are hard water stains? How do I clean/prevent them?
Okay that’s a lot of questions!
Hard water stains result from mineral presence in the water you put in your bong.
∙ You can clean them by doing a secondary clean with one tablespoon of lemon juice and enough water to reach the affected areas after you remove all the resin buildup.
∙ You can prevent them from happening by using distilled water as your bong water of choice for both cleaning and usage.
I’ve seen articles and forums discussing nail polish remover as a suitable replacement for isopropyl alcohol, is this true?
No. The chemicals used in nail polish remover not suitable for inhalation.
Can I damage my bong by using higher potency isopropyl alcohol?
Only cosmetically. Higher potency isopropyl can damage the paint on the outside of your bong. That’s why we recommend taking care to cover both holes before you start.
What is bong cleaner?

As cannabis continues to become more and more normalized, more bong cleaning solutions pop up in stores. If you have a hard time finding isopropyl or coarse salt, you can grab some bong cleaner like Red Eye Tek at Sunnyside (if you’re in Illinois).
How often should I clean my bong?

That depends on how much you use it. If it's used twice a week, you should clean it weekly. But if you rarely use it, then clean it when you see residue forming near the water line. The cleaner your bong, the more nuanced and tasty your smoking experience will be.
How often should I change the water in my bong?
For best results, you should empty the water in your bong after each sesh—to allow your piece to air dry between uses.

data.text: A Vape for Every Occasion

When most people think about vaping cannabis they think about a vape cart, but there are actually many more excellent options when it comes to how to consume! We'll dive into some of the more popular options.
A Vape for Every Occasion
Why Vape?

Even though the pot leaf is the most iconic symbol for cannabis, it’s not the leaves that we smoke to get the effects we want. The vast majority of the good things we are looking to consume are found in the trichomes of the plant—resinous glands that are highly concentrated on the flower of the cannabis plant. When you buy cannabis oil, you are buying a product that was created with the intention of removing all of the unwanted plant matter. The actual process of vaping involves heating that oil to a point where it turns into inhalable vapor. No unwanted smoke. No unwanted order. Just pure cannabis trichomes! When most people think about vaping cannabis, they think about a vape cart. What most people don’t realize is that they actually have a lot more options when it comes to how they choose to vape. So let’s take a quick look at some of the more popular options!
Vape Pens

Easily the most popular vaping setup. What makes these so great is their discretion and ease of use. Consuming oil is already going to be more discreet than smoking flower, but this is a system that can easily fit in your pocket or bag. It’s so discreet, in fact, that there is something to be said about how easy they can be to lose. Vape pens can either be an all-in-one disposable unit, or you can buy a rechargeable battery and replacement carts. Replacement carts are the more economical way to go, but sometimes you just want a disposable one for a specific event. As you can imagine, they are very popular at concerts. What’s great about the vape pen setup is that everything is together; however, like most supremely convenient things, you are going to be limited in functionality and have reliability issues. The biggest issue with oil carts is that they can fail and they can have a negative impact on the oil. Cannabis oil degrades over time—exposure to light, heat, and oxygen being the biggest causes. The heating element of the cart is really close to the oil reserve. This can create a situation where it is consistently warming the oil as you make your way through the cart. This is why many of the more expensive and proprietary vape tech carts tend to only come in half gram carts instead of the full gram. Full gram means there is a bigger chance it will fail at some point, also the half gram will keep its integrity better than a full gram. Sure you can find a full gram cart for $20 in some places, and there is a time and place for that; however, there are good reasons that quality oil and quality carts are the way they are. Cannabis enthusiasts can appreciate them.
Dab Pens

Unlike a vape pen, dab pens allow the consumer to use oil that is not in a cartridge. Cartridges are limited to viscous oils because the oil needs to be able to move through the cart. Dab pens give the consumer a lot more options when it comes to their oil selection because they can take any type of oil. To load a dab pen, you simply place oil in the chamber, attach the mouth piece, and take a pull like it's a vape pen. There used to be a time where these chambers were simply an attachment that you placed on top of your vape pen battery. This attachment was just coil that sat in the middle of a ceramic chamber. When you activate the dab pen, the coil would heat up the oil and create vapor. Nowadays the tech has gotten a lot better! Yes you can find attachments that will fit on top of your battery; however, now there are units specifically designed for this portable dabbing. They typically use a ceramic oven instead of a heating coil. This means that the oil is being heated evenly and avoiding extreme temperatures that can destroy the terpene profile. Dab pens are great products to have when you are on the go, but you still want to make sure you are getting the full experience from your cannabis. The cannaseurs’ choice for portable vaping.
Flower Vapes

Flower vapes were initially used like a bong. They were large, table-top devices that were convenient to nobody. These devices have a chamber that is loaded with ground flower. The chamber is then heated to a specific temperature (not high enough to combust the plant material), and the consumer can then enjoy freshly vaped trichomes right of the flower! Thankfully, the tech for flower vaporizers has advanced to the point where there are now handheld versions. These devices are primarily favored by people that do not want to use cannabis oils because they are wary of solvents and other production methods. Some people just prefer flower, and this is the best way to smoke flower if you also want the benefits of oil.

data.text: Dabbing

Dabbing is peak vaporizing. It’s the least convenient way to vape cannabis, as it is essentially deconstructed vaping; however, what is so great about dabbing is that the user has complete control over the process. What type of oil? How much oil will be consumed? At what temperature are you vaping? These are all decisions that will inform the ritual that frames your dabbing experience. The biggest upgrade for these units has to do with the heating element. Traditionally, a torch was used; however, now there are dab rigs that are completely electrical. A battery not only heats the device, but it can be programmed to heat to a specific temperature—sometimes from the convenience of an app on your phone! The addition of water filtration also sets this apart from other types of vaping. Dabbing is great for when vaping cannabis is the primary reason for vaping cannabis. It’s for when you have the time and space to really enjoy the moment. It’s the ultimate setup for a quality sesh when you’re with friends, or when you just want to do something special for yourself. So enjoy!

data.text: Common Ways to Consume Cannabis

Once you determine the kind of cannabis you want, it’s time to decide the way you’d like to consume it. With so many different ways to enjoy it these days, there’s a method to comfortably introduce cannabis into almost any lifestyle.
Each different method has its advantages depending on what experience you’re after. So, to give you a better idea of what we’re talking about, let's run through some of the most common ones.
Smoking

items: A classic way to consume cannabis
Smoked out of all types of devices
Cannabis is absorbed through the lungs
Onset: 7 minutes or less
Common Duration: 1–3 hours

data.text: Smoking is a classic way to enjoy cannabis and has been for generations. Even with all the other ways cannabis can be used, smoking is still one of the most common ways to enjoy the plant. Cannabis can be smoked in a number of different ways using a variety of devices like joints, pipes, bongs—even an apple .

To smoke cannabis, the dried flowers are lit and inhaled. The smoke fills the lungs where it is absorbed into the bloodstream. The effects from smoking cannabis are noticeable almost immediately and can last for a few hours*.

data.alt: Hand packing cannabis flower into a pipe.

data.text: Vaping

items: A convenient and discreet way to enjoy cannabis
Cannabis absorbed through the lungs
Onset: 7 minutes or less
Common Duration: 1–3 hours

data.text: Vaping, or vaporizing, is very similar to smoking with one key difference: instead of burning the cannabis, vaporization uses electronics to evenly heat cannabis or cannabis oil until a light vapor is released. The vapor is more discreet and much lighter than smoke because the plant matter is not completely burned.

Compared to smoking, vaping can produce more pronounced flavors because the gentle heat allows specific flavors to stand out without interference from hot or harsh smoke. The effects of vaping can feel more clear-headed compared to smoking and often less cannabis is needed to get the right feeling.
Eating

items: Absorbed through the liver
Strong effects
Consistent dosing
Onset: 30–90 min
Common duration: 1–6 hours

data.text: Most people agree that eating cannabis is completely different than smoking or vaping. A few of the key differences are that it’s smoke-free, it’s dosed differently, comes in many different flavors and forms, and the effects can feel stronger and last longer .

When you eat cannabis, it’s absorbed through your liver—which is a much slower process than when it enters the bloodstream through the lungs. It takes between 30 and 90 minutes for effects to start, so be patient.
Once they do hit, the effects of edibles are typically stronger and may last longer because your body metabolizes it in a way that affects the central nervous system more efficiently.

data.alt: Edible gummies in a bowl next to a cup of tea.

data.text: Oral Ingestion

items: Absorbed through the liver
Targeted effects
Consistent dosing
Onset: 30–90 min
Common duration: 4–6 hours

data.text: Taking cannabis orally, like in capsules or tablets, is a similar experience to eating it. The THC or CBD is absorbed through your liver before entering your bloodstream so the onset can take some time before noticed. Like edibles, it’s best to be patient.
Oral ingestion is discreet, can be easily added to a medication or wellness routine, and dosing is formulated to target more specific and consistent effects and experiences.
Sublingual

items: Common with tinctures
Rapidly enters the bloodstream through blood vessels under the tongue
Onset: 7 minutes or less
Common duration: 2–4 hours or more

data.text: Tinctures are the most common way that cannabis is consumed sublingually. Though tinctures can be added to food or drink, which allows them to function more like an edible, many choose to drop the liquid directly under the tongue, absorbing rapidly through the blood vessels in the mouth.
Start with the recommended dosing on the package. The effects are typically noticed within minutes and generally last for a few hours, slowly tapering off over time.
Topical

items: Fast-acting, localized effects
No intoxicating effects (except some transdermal products)
Absorbs into the skin

data.text: Cannabis topicals are different because they do not create the same rush of euphoria that most other cannabis products provide. When you apply infused lotions and balms to the skin they give effects directly to the area and most often do not create intoxicating effects.
Topicals may be a great option for those that don’t want to be slowed down by everyday aches and pains.

title: Why Cannabis Legalization has its Roots in Racial Justice
description: We're delving into the history of cannabis with a lens on how racism has contributed to creating our country and its current culture.

data.text: America’s cannabis prohibition laws were enacted on a foundation of fear, ignorance, and racism, with vast racial disparities in the enforcement and policies that have hit Black and Brown communities the hardest. A 2020 analysis by the American Civil Liberties Union concluded that Black people are 3.6 times more likely than white people to be arrested for cannabis possession despite blacks and whites using cannabis at nearly the same rate.

“The War on Drugs has not been a war on drugs, it's been a war on people, and disproportionately people of color and low-income individuals,” said Sen. Cory Booker (D-NJ) when introducing The Marijuana Justice Act . “The end we seek is not just legalization, it's justice.”

To better comprehend the current state of social justice in the cannabis industry, it’s worth looking at the foundational racism built into prohibition and acknowledge the work of countless social justice activists fighting for equality through cannabis-related causes.
Harry Anslinger and the Marihuana Tax Act of 1937

Cannabis first entered the US after the turn of the 20th century by two primary avenues: Caribbean immigrants and sailors arriving in New Orleans as well as Mexican citizens escaping the violence of the Mexican Revolution. As marginalized Black and Brown people began to embrace cannabis for recreational purposes, Americans who were sympathetic to racist ideologies adopted bigoted stereotypes about cannabis use, eventually leading to its prohibition in the 1930s.

Ushering in an era of Reefer Madness propaganda, Harry Anslinger, the first commissioner of the Federal Bureau of Narcotics serving five Presidents from Hoover to Kennedy, is largely credited with turning the nation against cannabis via fear-mongering tactics and racist rhetoric.

In a 1937 article appearing in The American Magazine, the drug czar wrote: “no one knows, when he places a marijuana cigarette to his lips, whether he will become a joyous reveller in a musical heaven, a mad insensate, a calm philosopher, or a murderer.”
Anslinger added cannabis to the nation’s drug control laws, bringing the plant under federal control, and was the architect of The Marihuana Tax Act of 1937 which formally began prohibition.

data.text: Richard Nixon and America’s War on Drugs

In 1971, President Nixon stoked anti-BIPOC sentiment with his declaration of a War on Drugs, a campaign built on militarized over-policing, an egregious racial bias, and, ultimately, wasted time and taxpayer dollars. The War on Drugs drastically increased the size and presence of federal drug control agencies while racially targeted measures were passed like mandatory sentencing and no-knock warrants.

President Nixon rescheduled cannabis as a Schedule One drug — the most restrictive category of drugs defined as having no medical benefits — pending review by a commission he appointed led by Republican Pennsylvania Governor Raymond Shafer. In 1972, the Shafer Commission unanimously recommended decriminalizing the possession and distribution of cannabis for personal use, but Nixon outright rejected its recommendations, thereby stifling medical research into cannabis for decades to come.

Later on in 2016, a top Nixon aide, John Ehrlichman would tell Harper’s Magazine , "The Nixon campaign in 1968, and the Nixon White House after that, had two enemies: the antiwar left and black people. You understand what I’m saying? We knew we couldn’t make it illegal to be either against the war or black, but by getting the public to associate the hippies with marijuana and blacks with heroin, and then criminalizing both heavily, we could disrupt those communities. We could arrest their leaders, raid their homes, break up their meetings, and vilify them night after night on the evening news. Did we know we were lying about the drugs? Of course we did." Mandatory minimums served to further criminalize communities of color as Nixon’s movement exploded the US prison population disproportionately affecting Black and Latinx people over nonviolent crimes.
Ronald Reagan: Just Say ‘No’

In 1986, President Ronald Reagan chose to double down on Nixon’s War on Drugs, promising Americans a future drug-free generation after signing The Anti-Drug Abuse Act into law. President Reagan insisted the legislation would give those with substance abuse issues the means to “live right” and not fill jails with drug crime offenders. Yet, the opposite happened as “tough on crime” laws encouraged judges to hand out harsh sentences for simple possession and low-level cannabis sales.

“Drug dealers were made into monsters, the sole reason neighborhoods and major cities were failing,” says Jay-Z in his Drug Policy Alliance short The War on Drugs: From Prohibition to Gold Rush . “No one wanted to talk about Reaganomics and the ending of social safety nets, the defunding of schools and the loss of jobs in cities across America. Young men like me who hustled became the sole villain.”

data.text: Modern Day Advocates for Change
Wanda James

Wanda James is known for founding the first Black-owned legal cannabis dispensary in the US, Simply Pure, along with her partner Scott Durrah. James, a military veteran and former Navy lieutenant, also worked on the National Finance Committee for President Obama. The entrepreneur has built a thriving cannabis business in Denver while remaining a powerful advocate for equity and empowering other Black business owners.
Cory Booker

Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) is a Black legislator using his positions of power to advance a landmark bill that would end the federal prohibition on marijuana, expunge records, and reinvest in communities most impacted by the War on Drugs. "The Marijuana Justice Act seeks to reverse decades of this unfair, unjust, and failed policy by removing marijuana from the list of controlled substances and making it legal at the federal level," said Booker.
Dr. Chanda Masias

Dr. Chanda Masias is the Owner and General Manager of the National Holistic Healing Center Medical Marijuana Dispensary (NHHC) in Washington D.C. For over 15 years, Dr. Masias has been driven by her passion for education, bettering the lives of patients, and empowering women and minorities in the industry. She is also the medical marijuana cultivator and processor for the state of Louisiana and Chairwoman of the Board of Managers and CEO for Women Grow, empowering the next generation of women leaders in the cannabis and hemp industry.
Nadir Pearson

Nadir Pearson is the Founder of StudentMMJ.com as well as an impassioned content creator, digital strategist, and speaker with a passion for cannabis advocacy. While at Brown University, Nadir launched the Student Marijuana Alliance for Research and Transparency (SMART), a college cannabis community striving to make positive social reforms in the industry.
Alphonso T. Blunt, Jr. and Brittany Moore

Brittany Moore and Alphonso “Tucky” Blunt Jr. opened the first equity marijuana dispensary in Oakland, appropriately named after the founders, “Blunts + Moore.” The founders worked in the cannabis industry for years before opening the dispensary with Blunt, a lifetime Oakland resident striving to open his own dispensary since 1999 and Moore, the general manager of dispensaries in Colorado and California and an active member of the Minority Cannabis Business Association, NORML, and Women Grow.
A Path Forward: Social Equity and Social Justice in Cannabis

The effects of cannabis prohibition and racial bias are still experienced in communities of color today. Those affected are still facing barriers to participating in the legalized cannabis industry - an industry that wouldn't exist without them.

The world of cannabis edibles can seem pretty daunting to newcomers, but fear not, friend— we’re here to help highlight the key facts and dispel some of the misconceptions around edibles, so you can decide if they’re right for you.
What exactly is an edible?
Simply put, an edible is any food or beverage that’s been infused with highly concentrated cannabis extract.
What are THC and CBD gummies?

THC and CBD gummies are some of our most popular cannabis edible products, available in sativa, indica, and hybrid formulations. Here's an explainer on how THC and CBD effects differ. We offer conveniently-dosed, discreet, and convenient gummy flavors and formulations designed to fit your lifestyle. The typical dosage values are 2.5, 5, and 10mg.
Is eating cannabis different than smoking it?
Most people agree that eating cannabis is a completely different experience than smoking or vaping it. Here are some of the key differences:
It’s smoke-free.
One obvious difference is there’s no smoke or vapor to deal with, and there’s no need for additional tools, which make it a popular choice for simple, discreet cannabis use.
It’s dosed differently.
Smoking or vaping is something you measure by the amount you inhale. Pre-packaged edibles are measured by the amount you ingest, right down to the milligram.
It comes in familiar flavors and forms.

For people who dislike the taste of smoking or vaping cannabis, edibles provide you with a variety of delicious flavors and familiar forms—like gummies and cookies— to make your experience more enjoyable.
It can take longer to kick in.

When you eat cannabis, it’s absorbed through your liver—which is a much slower process than when it enters the bloodstream through the lungs. Most report that it takes between 30 and 90 minutes for effects to be noticed. Be patient!
It can have a stronger, longer effect.
Once they do hit, the effects of edibles are typically stronger and may last longer because your body metabolizes it in a way that affects the central nervous system more efficiently.

Enjoying your edible experience.
Clear your schedule.
Effects can last more than 6 hours. Edibles are more enjoyable if you don’t have responsibilities to worry about.

Make sure you’re in a good mindset, in good company and are generally comfortable with your surroundings.
Start low (2.5mg dose) and go slow.

The best way to stay in control is to give yourself the chance to check in before going any further. Start with a low dosage and wait at least an hour or so to feel the full effect before having any more.

First, remember that you aren’t the first person to overdo it with edibles. It will pass with time.

Tips for Enjoying Cannabis Oil in the Summer

For many cannabis enthusiasts, it is hard to beat quality flower. There’s just something magical about breaking down the perfect bud and preparing it for consumption—the loud smells, the sticky texture, the ritual rolling or packing, and, finally, the moment you light up and enjoy all that hard work. It’s all very satisfying.

There will always be a place for enjoying flower, but it’s not always going to be your best option. Especially when you’re on the go! Sometimes you don’t want to draw attention to yourself, spend the time rolling up (we all can’t have full-time blunt rollers like Snoop), or carry around pipes. Sometimes you want something simple and discrete. Cannabis oil can be exactly that!

Cannabis oil (also called cannabis concentrate) has become so popular over the last few decades that it even has its own holiday. Whereas 4/20 is the official holiday of all things cannabis, 7/10 is a holiday exclusively dedicated to cannabis oil. Why 7/10? Because someone noticed that if you flip 710 upside down, it spells “OIL.” That’s it. Maybe not the most exciting origin story, but it’s no less of a reason to celebrate!

710 falls right in the middle of the summer—a prime time to enjoy cannabis when you are out doing your favorite activities. Let’s take a closer look at your different options for consuming cannabis oil and how you might utilize them to elevate your summer activities!
Vapes
No product is more synonymous with cannabis oil than a vape cartridge. When it comes to inhaling cannabis, there is nothing more discrete or easier to use.

One of the best advantages of vaping instead of smoking is that the smell won’t linger. If you smoke a joint, everyone within a block radius knows you are smoking a joint. Even after you're done smoking the joint, that smell is going to be wafting off of you for hours.

Yes, cannabis vapor is going to smell (especially if it is a high quality oil ); however, it’s not going to be overpowering or leave you smelling like a pound of cannabis. Some cannabis vape systems also look a lot like non-cannabis devices. In other words, it’s easier to blend into the crowd with a vape pen than a joint. There is also something to be said about not having a hot joint and smoke swirling around you in the summer when you are already hot and sweaty.

data.alt: woman consuming cannabis through a vape cartridge

data.text: Edibles
710 is mostly associated with cannabis oil that is vaporized, but what do you think the cannabis element is in your favorite edibles? I’ll give you a hint: it’s cannabis oil.

It’s not going to mimic the feeling of smoking a joint, and the effects of an edible are going to be vastly different from the experience you get from inhaling cannabis vapor since they have a much longer onset time. It’s the same oil though - just activated!

Not everyone that enjoys cannabis likes, or has the ability, to inhale cannabis vapor. For these people, edibles are the best path toward meeting their cannabis goals. Also, if 710 really is a holiday to celebrate cannabis oil, why not celebrate all the products that include cannabis oil? Let’s keep an open mind!

And talk about being discreet -- there might be a minor cannabis aroma emanating from an unpackaged edible, but there is no cannabis smell that is the direct result of it being consumed. It won’t look like a cannabis product, as the oil is hidden in the edible. With the longer onset time you can even eat or drink it before you go out, so you can avoid having it out in public entirely.
They even have cannabis-infused ice cream now! Cannabis oil really is amazing in its versatility.
Dabs

Dabbing cannabis certainly isn’t as discrete as a vape cartridge; however, it does still have a certain allure. Since it is pretty much deconstructed vaping, it still has the advantage of not leaving a huge odor behind; however, it does require some equipment in order to function.
For a long time dabbing was pretty much limited to stationary places, as you needed a whole setup to make it work; however, new advances in cannabis tech has enabled dabbing to become more mobile!

The most discrete version is going to be a dab pen. These are a little larger than vaping pens; however, instead of taking cartridges, they employ heating elements that vaporize cannabis oil that is placed on them by the consumer manually. The biggest benefit of this way of consuming is that you are not limited to oils that are in cartridges. You can use whatever type of oil you want!

The rise of electronic dab rigs has also made dabbing portable. It’s not nearly as small as a dab pen, but they typically have more features (temperature control, water filtration, etc.) and, for this reason, the preferred method of vaping for the serious cannabis oil devotee.
Proper Storage

Like all cannabis products, you should take measures in making sure they are stored properly. Heat and light are two things that will degrade your cannabis products rather quickly—two things that are very abundant during the summer.

Make sure to keep your cannabis products in a dry, cool place whenever possible. Cannabis cartridges can be particularly sensitive, and the last thing you want to happen is to get to your location only to find that your vape is broken. So be gentle with your cannabis!
Tips for the Summer!
Now that you know about your options for consuming cannabis oil, you can pick the perfect product to compliment your summer activities.

Are you looking to enjoy a day at the pool or the beach with some friends to beat the heat? Maybe a small vape pen can fit in that waterproof pouch you brought for your phone, or maybe you want to avoid bringing electronics with you altogether and just enjoy a nice edible. The last thing you might want is a lit joint near your inflatable raft.

Maybe you are looking to enjoy a festival. Cannabis is great for enhancing the live music experience or making delicious food taste even more delicious. Whatever your fest of choice, a small vape pen with your preferred strain is going to be the perfect complement as you wander throughout the crowds in search of reasonably priced water.

Or maybe you are looking to savor the great outdoors and go on a camping trip. Sure you could bring some flower, but this is a post about celebrating cannabis oil! Camping is the perfect environment for pretty much anything cannabis. A nice vape to take with you on a hike, an edible to help you nap in a hammock to recover from the hike or passing the electronic dab rig around the campfire at night as you consume smore after smore.
When it comes to consuming cannabis oil, you are only really limited by your imagination!
